mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between RSAFS drops and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over three months signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals strengthening supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth accelerates.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three months indicates strengthening demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing market drives economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite the signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) is rising faster than 2% annually, the combination signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% over the same month, the combined signal indicates a tightening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter signals strengthening economic demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth accelerate.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between GDPC1 increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
